method: Read-only source/diff/control-flow review. No code execution, native compilation, tests, timing or repository edits by reviewer.
scope: Dispatcher quarantine, idempotent release, rollback/close lifecycle
Five newly authored actual-child fault tests and one pure denominator negative
Changed documentation and direct observer caller boundary
positive_findings: A normal direct-child wait failure creates explicit recoverable cleanup ownership rather than releasing dispatch references.
Per-call identities make successful recovery release at most once; rollback/close retain a quarantined version while its call count is nonzero.
Retries do not execute the native entry or signal a possibly reused PGID again.
Diagnostic recovery preserves the earlier failure; it cannot retrospectively turn the observation into success.
Popen success is separately recorded from positive HIA entry evidence; setup failures and missing outcomes remain unavailable.
New fault tests withhold confirmation only after real exit observed through WNOWAIT, then use the original Popen.wait to reap the same child.
No immediate cyclic lock ordering found: try_reap releases cleanup lock before dispatcher release and probe callback.

issues.finding: Quarantine depends on NativeChildCleanupPending remaining the propagated exception. A descriptor close OSError in the diagnostic outer finally can mask Pending, leaving _cleanup.confirmed false but _quarantined false; _run then takes generic except and releases the call. Ordinary temporary-file context exit can analogously mask Pending before execute catches it.
issues.suggested_resolution: Base the outermost release decision on retained cleanup ownership/confirmation, preserve auxiliary close errors separately, and add a failure control for a parent finalizer error after withheld reap confirmation.

issues.finding: try_reap validates its timeout but acquires a plain blocking Lock while another caller may hold that lock through process.wait(timeout=2). A simultaneous retry_cleanup(timeout=0) or close(wait=True,timeout=0.02) can wait beyond its caller deadline before its own wait begins. This does not itself release resources early; it contradicts bounded-deadline behavior.
issues.suggested_resolution: Bound or avoid lock acquisition and recompute remaining time before process.wait; cover two concurrent retry callers. Keep cleanup safety separate from wall-time guarantees.

boundary_notes.finding: The direct comparison propagates NativeChildCleanupPending and therefore emits no successful receipt, but always closes its own pinned descriptor. A caller that serializes/drops the exception also drops the explicit cleanup recovery handle; unlike NativeVersionDispatcher it provides no persistent quarantine inventory. Child-side inherited descriptors remain owned by the child.
boundary_notes.scope: Do not generalize dispatcher drain guarantees to standalone direct-observer clients. Either document the required retained exception.cleanup contract or add an explicit owner boundary for those consumers.
